docs.title: SimSight Companion
docs.text:
Play The Sims 4 with a screen reader, on the Mac or Windows, and from your phone.

SimSight speaks menus, dialogs, tooltips, notifications and what your Sim is doing: with the macOS voices on the Mac, through NVDA or JAWS on Windows. A phone app (made for VoiceOver on the iPhone) shows the household, the needs, what happens, and lets you play: pause, actions, the house, the Sims, the game's questions.

Made for playing together, a sighted player on the mouse and a blind player hearing what happens, and for playing alone with the keyboard and the phone.

Alpha

SimSight is early. The Mac version is played regularly; the newest parts of the phone app are still being tried. Windows is new and not yet tried inside the game: Windows testers are wanted.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Install: one command on the Mac or Windows, the game closed.
  2. Start the game and load a household. The accessibility menu opens with Option+Command+A on the Mac, Control+Alt+H on Windows.
  3. Connect your phone: in that menu, phone companion. Scan the QR code or type the code it says in the app. Then read the phone guide.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
• Phone app: every screen, with VoiceOver.
  • Mac: keyboard, commands, a fixed phone address, a meeting point, asking an AI helper.
  • Windows: getting started, controls and options.
  • Help us test: what to try and how to tell us.

docs.title: Based on TS4 Access
docs.text: SimSight is an independent project based on TS4 Access, the screen-reader mod for The Sims 4 by tyjokr, LeonianUniverse and contributors (MIT licence). See About for the credits.

docs.title: About
docs.text: SimSight Companion is an independent project based on TS4 Access, the screen-reader mod for The Sims 4. It was started so a blind player and a sighted player could play together on a Mac, and grew a phone app and a Windows version.

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
Everyone whose work is in TS4 Access:

  • tyjokr: creator of TS4 Access.
  • LeonianUniverse: lead developer of TS4 Access; also the world scanner, tile cursor and object placement (from his a11yscan mod).
  • Michael Maslo: TS4 Access Plus (Alt-key readouts, reminders, Sim creation without Create a Sim, the Build helper).
  • DaRainbowGirlXX: Build cursor and scanner additions, house building, roofs, basements, lot planning and many screen-reader fixes.

The full list is in CONTRIBUTORS.md.

docs.title: Licences
docs.text:
• SimSight and TS4 Access: MIT.
  • Speech on Windows: Prism by Ethin Probst, MPL-2.0, shipped unmodified.
  • The phone tunnel: cloudflared by Cloudflare, Apache-2.0, shipped unmodified.

docs.title: Not affiliated
docs.text: SimSight is a fan-made mod. It is not made, endorsed or supported by Electronic Arts or Maxis. The Sims is a trademark of Electronic Arts Inc.

docs.title: Source
docs.text: Everything is on GitHub: the mod, the phone app, the companion and these guides.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Quit The Sims 4 first. Both installers back up your game settings and saves before changing anything, allow mods in the game settings, and can be run again to update or remove SimSight. Your saves are never changed.

New to The Sims 4? Start the game once and quit it, so it creates its settings, then install.

docs.title: Mac
docs.text:
Open Terminal (Command+Space, type Terminal, Return), paste this line and press Return:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/releases/latest/download/install.sh | zsh

It says each step (VoiceOver reads them; with VoiceOver off, the Mac voice says them) and asks you to press Return before installing.

Without Terminal: download SimSight-Companion-mac.zip from the latest release and double-click Install SimSight Companion.command. macOS may say it cannot verify the developer: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, find the message near the bottom, choose Open Anyway, then double-click it again.

docs.title: Windows (alpha)
docs.text:
Open PowerShell (Windows+X, then Terminal), paste this line and press Enter:

irm https://github.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

It writes each step as a line your screen reader reads, finds your Sims 4 folder (OneDrive and other languages too), checks the download and installs the mod with its speech pack for NVDA and JAWS.

Without PowerShell: download SimSight-Companion-windows.zip from the latest release, extract it and open Install SimSight Companion.cmd. If Windows says it protected your PC, choose More info, then Run anyway.

Then: getting started on Windows.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
In the game, open the accessibility menu, choose companion setup, then Check for updates. With the game running, the update is downloaded and installed when you quit the game; with the game closed, it is installed at once. The game also tells you when a new version is out.

Or quit the game and run the install line again.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
• Mac: run the install line with -s uninstall at the end, or double-click Uninstall SimSight Companion.command from the zip.
  • Windows: run the install line again and type r.

The mod folder goes to SimSight Backups, next to your saves; your saves are not touched.

docs.title: What gets installed
docs.text:
Everything goes in Mods/SimSight, in your Sims 4 user folder:

  • the mod itself (SimSight.ts4script) and the game interface it needs (SimSight_UI.package, from TS4 Access);
  • the phone companion (simsight-bridge), which serves the phone app;
  • Cloudflare's tunnel program (cloudflared), which lets the phone reach the computer from any network;
  • on the Mac, the voice helper (simsight-say); on Windows, the speech pack for screen readers (Prism).

The installer's download is checked against its SHA-256 fingerprint before anything is installed.

docs.title: Testers wanted
docs.text: SimSight is in alpha. It is played regularly on a Mac, by a sighted player and a blind player on an iPhone with VoiceOver. We need more people to try it, and above all Windows players.

docs.title: Windows testers
docs.text:
The Windows version has not been played inside the game yet. If you play The Sims 4 on Windows with NVDA or JAWS (or would like to), you can help a lot with one evening:

  1. Install it (one PowerShell line; it backs up your settings and saves first, and can remove SimSight again).
  2. Start your screen reader, then the game, and load a household.
  3. Tell us what happens, even if it is only "nothing speaks". The first minutes matter most:
    • Does the game start with the mod? Does anything speak?
    • Does Control+Alt+H open the accessibility menu?
    • Does phone companion open a page and say a code?
    • Does the phone app connect, and show your household?

docs.title: Mac and phone testers
docs.text: The test checklist lists what to try, screen by screen. Lines marked new have only been checked outside the game so far.

docs.title: How to tell us
docs.text:
• On GitHub: open a test report. The form asks for the computer, the screen reader and what happened; every field is optional except the description.
  • Without a GitHub account: in the Discord where you found SimSight.

For each problem, the most useful is: where you were, what you pressed, and what was said (word for word if you can). If the game itself showed an error, the file SimSight.log in Mods/SimSight helps too: it lists what the mod said and did. It contains your Sims' names; nothing else personal.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Your saves are never changed. The installer copies them to SimSight Backups before installing anything.
  • Removing SimSight moves it out of the Mods folder; the game works as before.
  • The phone link is a key: anyone with it can play on your game. Send it only to your own phone. Disconnect every phone in companion setup makes a new key if you shared it by mistake.

docs.title: SimSight console commands (Mac)
docs.text:
You do not need these for normal play: Option+Command+A opens the accessibility menu, and the phone app does most of the rest. The keyboard is in KEYBOARD.md.

Open the game's console with Command+Shift+C (Control+Shift+C on some keyboards), type a command, press Return. Close the console with the same keys before using menus.

docs.title: Help and settings
docs.text:
• simsight.hub: the accessibility menu.
  • simsight.companion: the phone link page (QR code and pairing code).
  • simsight.setup: SimSight setup on the Mac (phone address, meeting point, disconnect every phone).
  • simsight.menu window: the settings window (simplified menus, Build controls).
  • simsight.settings: read the current settings.
  • simsight.reload: apply changes made by hand to SimSight.cfg.
  • simsight.scannermode on: scanner browsing with the arrow keys.
  • simsight.keys on: keyboard navigation of menus and panels.
  • simsight.simactions on: announce what the active Sim starts doing.
  • simsight.objectnames on: read the names of objects in the world.
  • simsight.captions on: show the spoken text on screen.

Use off instead of on to turn an option off.

docs.title: Speech
docs.text:
• simsight.speechmode hover: read what the pointer is on, automatically.
  • simsight.speechmode manual: read only when asked.
  • simsight.speechmode off: silence (Option+Command+S does the same).
  • simsight.tooltipdelay 1.5: wait 1.5 seconds before longer descriptions.
  • simsight.voice rate 3 (-10 to 10), simsight.voice volume 70 (0 to 100), simsight.voice name Thomas (part of a macOS voice name). Better voices: System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content > System voice > Manage Voices.

docs.title: Quick access
docs.text:
• simsight.phonelist: the Sim's phone actions.
  • simsight.phone: answer a waiting call or text.
  • simsight.household: choose the active Sim.
  • simsight.contacts: known contacts.
  • simsight.funds: household funds.
  • simsight.scan rescan: refresh the scanner.
  • simsight.log: diagnostic log on or off (Mods/SimSight/SimSight.log).

Settings commands are saved; updating the mod keeps SimSight.cfg.

docs.title: Optional: a fixed address for the phone app
docs.text:
By default the phone link uses a random Cloudflare address that changes every time the game starts, so the QR code must be scanned again each session and a Home Screen app stops working. With a fixed address, the phone keeps the same link: add it to the Home Screen once and open it like an app.

You need a free Cloudflare account and a domain managed by Cloudflare. No domain? A meeting point gives the app a fixed address too, with only a free account.

docs.title: Set up (once)
docs.text:
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard: Zero Trust > Networks > Tunnels > Create a tunnel, type Cloudflared, give it a name (for example sims).
  2. On the install page, copy the token (the long text after --token in the commands shown). Do not run those commands: the mod runs the tunnel itself while the game is open.
  3. Public hostname: choose a subdomain, for example sims.example.com, service HTTP, URL localhost:47800. Save.
  4. Open SimSight setup: in game, accessibility menu (Option+Command+A) > companion setup; with the game closed, double-click SimSight Setup.command in the Mods/SimSight folder. Choose Fixed address, paste the token (the whole command is fine) and type the public hostname, then Save. If the game was running, quit and restart it.
  5. Start the game. Once a household is loaded the Mac says "Phone link ready…"; the QR code (Option+Command+A, phone companion) now shows the fixed address. Scan it once, then Share > Add to Home Screen. If the Home Screen app ever says Pair this phone, choose phone companion on the Mac and type the 6-digit code it says: no scanning needed.

docs.title: Or from the command line
docs.text:
With cloudflared logged in to your account (cloudflared tunnel login):

cloudflared tunnel create simsight
cloudflared tunnel route dns simsight sims.example.com
cloudflared tunnel token simsight     # the token to paste in SimSight setup

No public hostname needed in the dashboard: the mod sends everything the tunnel receives to the phone app.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The phone still needs the pairing key that the QR code carries: knowing the address alone is not enough to see or control the game.
  • For an extra lock, Cloudflare Access can ask for an email code before the page opens (Zero Trust > Access > Applications).
  • To go back to random addresses: SimSight setup > Changing address.
  • The settings live in ~/Library/Application Support/SimSightCompanion/config.json (the setup page writes it). It holds secrets: do not share it.

docs.title: A ChatGPT helper for SimSight on Mac
docs.text: Ask ChatGPT (or any assistant) about the mod and its phone app, in your language, with VoiceOver-friendly steps. The assistant reads the guides from GitHub each time, so it follows the docs as they change.

docs.title: Easiest: from the phone app
docs.text: Help tab > Ask an AI: Open ChatGPT starts a conversation with the request already filled in; Copy the prompt works with any assistant. Works with free accounts, nothing to set up.

docs.title: Your own helper in ChatGPT (optional)
docs.text: Custom GPTs are being retired by OpenAI (December 2026) and replaced by plugins. A plugin is personal (it starts private, without a share link), so each person makes their own; the content below is the same for every route.

docs.title: As a ChatGPT plugin
docs.text:
Quickest: in ChatGPT's Work mode, ask Plugin Creator to create a plugin from this spec and send it the link https://github.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/blob/main/docs/mac/PLUGIN.md (it reads the name, workflow, integrations and examples from there).

By hand:

  1. In ChatGPT, open GPTs (or Plugins) and choose Create plugin.
  2. Name and description: use the Name and Description blocks below.
  3. Add a skill (the plugin's instructions) and paste the Instructions block below.
  4. If the editor allows web search or browsing, turn it on: the plugin then reads the current guides each time and never needs updating.
  5. If it does not, upload these files as reference files (download each link with "Save as"), and upload them again when the guides change:
  6. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/llms.txt
  7. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/docs/mac/PHONE-GUIDE.md
  8. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/docs/mac/KEYBOARD.md
  9. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/mac/PLAYERS.md
  10. Save, then open it in the ChatGPT app on the phone to use it with VoiceOver.

The guides' history on GitHub (docs/mac) shows when they changed.

docs.title: As a ChatGPT Project
docs.text:
1. In ChatGPT, create a Project (for example "SimSight").
  2. Open the project's instructions and paste the Instructions block below.
  3. Make sure web search is allowed in that project, so it can read the guides.
  4. Ask questions inside the project.

Name, Description and Conversation starters are optional for a Project.

docs.title: Name
docs.text: SimSight Companion helper

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Help with SimSight on Mac: the Sims 4 accessibility mod and its phone app for VoiceOver. Answers in your language.

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
You help people play The Sims 4 on a Mac with the SimSight accessibility mod and its phone companion app. Many users are blind or low vision and use VoiceOver on an iPhone; often a sighted player plays on the Mac at the same time.

At the start of every conversation, before answering, open and read:
1. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/llms.txt
2. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/docs/mac/PHONE-GUIDE.md
If these guides were given to you as reference files instead, use those, and say when an answer might be out of date. Read other files listed in llms.txt when the question needs them (Mac keyboard: docs/mac/KEYBOARD.md; installing: mac/PLAYERS.md; fixed address: docs/mac/FIXED-ADDRESS.md). These files are the source of truth and change often: always use the current version, never memory. If you cannot open them, say so and answer carefully from general knowledge, marking what you are unsure of.

How to answer:
- Answer in the user's language (often Spanish or French). Keep the app's screen and button names as the app shows them in that language when you know them; otherwise give the English name in quotes.
- Give short, numbered steps a screen reader user can follow: screen (tab) names, headings, button names, swipes ("swipe right to the button …, double-tap"). Never rely on colours, icons or positions on screen.
- One task at a time. Ask what they see or hear if something does not match the guide.
- Game object and action names come from the game, usually in English (for example "Quick Meal", "Grab a Plate").
- For problems the guide does not cover, suggest the "When something goes wrong" section, or reporting the problem to the person who installed the mod.
- Do not invent features. If the guide does not mention something, say it is not in the app yet.
- Never ask for or repeat pairing links, tokens or the contents of config.json: they are private keys to the game.

docs.title: Conversation starters
docs.text:
How do I start playing with the phone app?
¿Cómo hago que mi Sim coma?
Comment savoir où sont les pièces de la maison ?
What can I do when the game asks me a question?

docs.title: Test it
docs.text: Ask one of the starters. The answer should mention screens such as Live, Play or House and say it read the guide. If it answers without reading, check that web search is allowed.

docs.title: SimSight keyboard on a Mac
docs.text:
SimSight's keyboard on the Mac (Windows keys in brackets). The keys are taken only while The Sims 4 is the front app, so other apps, macOS and VoiceOver keep their own shortcuts. Letters follow the letters printed on your keyboard (AZERTY, QWERTZ...).

Windows Mac Ctrl+Alt+key Control+Shift+key (⌃⇧) Alt+key (SimSight Plus) Option+Shift+key (⌥⇧) Alt+Shift+arrow (drawing cursor, 5 m) Option+Shift+Command+arrow Ctrl+Shift+N (needs) Control+Shift+N Arrows, Tab, Enter, Space, Backspace, Esc in menus and the scanner the same keys

Always on the Mac: Option+Command+A opens the SimSight menu, Option+Command+S turns the speech on or off.

docs.title: On by default, and turning navigation on
docs.text: The information keys (Control+Shift and Option+Shift) always work. Moving through menus, dialogs and pickers with the arrows, Tab and Enter, and the scanner, are off by default on the Mac (the sighted player uses the mouse): turn keyboard navigation on in the SimSight settings menu (Option+Command+A, settings menu), or type simsight.keys on in the cheat console (Command+Shift+C). Bare keys are only taken while the mod owns them (a menu or dialog is open, scanner mode is on, or the Build cursor is active); otherwise the game gets them as usual.

docs.title: Control+Shift keys (Ctrl+Alt on Windows)
docs.text: Key Action ⌃⇧ Up / Down previous / next (scanner, or the open menu) ⌃⇧ Left / Right previous / next category ⌃⇧ Page Up / Page Down previous / next subcategory ⌃⇧ Return open the menu / activate ⌃⇧ Space scanner mode on or off ⌃⇧ Delete back / close ⌃⇧ S / W / R refresh the scanner / where am I / repeat ⌃⇧ H help (the accessibility menu) ⌃⇧ C day and time ⌃⇧ P waiting call or text ⌃⇧ E / G mood and moodlets / wants and fears ⌃⇧ Q action queue ⌃⇧ L diagnostic logging on or off ⌃⇧ V running events ⌃⇧ M / K milestones / character values ⌃⇧ O / I Buy catalog / search the catalog (Build mode) ⌃⇧ 1 to 8 control household Sim 1 to 8 ⌃⇧ N needs ⌃⇧ B / T / F Build placement / read-only grid / aim at a grid point ⌃⇧ U / D / J layer up / layer down / label the room ⌃⇧ , / . smaller / larger scanner range ⌃⇧ [ / ] rotate left / right ⌃⇧ Z / Y / X undo / redo / sell

docs.title: Option+Shift keys (Alt on Windows, SimSight Plus)
docs.text:
Key Action ⌥⇧ A SimSight Plus menu ⌥⇧ Q action queue ⌥⇧ N needs ⌥⇧ L last notifications ⌥⇧ T time and day ⌥⇧ R rooms ⌥⇧ W where am I ⌥⇧ C create and edit Sims ⌥⇧ B build helper ⌥⇧ arrows (⌘ for 5 m) drawing cursor ⌥⇧ X / S / Z / D drawing cursor: where / mark start / undo / draw

Not on the Mac yet: the main menu and Create a Sim keys (before a save is loaded), the build tools that move the real mouse, and numpad navigation.

docs.title: Optional: a meeting point for the phone app
docs.text:
Without anything set up, the phone link is a random Cloudflare address that changes each game session (scan the QR code or type the pairing code each time). A meeting point gives the phone app one fixed address, for good, and the app then finds your Mac by itself every session:

  • Open the app from the Home Screen, before or after starting the game: it says "Waiting for the game", then connects by itself.
  • Several Macs with the same phone: Settings > Computers lists them; the app connects to whichever has the game running.
  • You only need a free Cloudflare account, no domain.

The meeting point is a small Cloudflare Worker, like a URL shortener whose target changes each session. You deploy your own, or use one someone shares. It only keeps, for each computer: an ID, today's tunnel address, and while a pairing code is shown, that code hashed (5 minutes). No names, no game data, never the pairing key. After the phone has the address, it talks to the computer through its tunnel; the meeting point is out of the way.

Several meeting points, and when one stops: the setup page takes a list (one per line); the computer announces itself to each. The phone app asks each meeting point in its own list (Settings > Meeting points, where you can add another). If none answers, the app opens anyway (it keeps a copy) and says so: open the link from the computer to play, or add another meeting point. Nothing else breaks.

Pairing codes have 9 digits with meeting points (spoken in three groups), so codes of many computers at a shared meeting point do not clash and cannot be guessed. Guessing is also limited per network and for everyone together.

docs.title: Set up (once)
docs.text:
You need Node.js on the Mac (https://nodejs.org) and the SimSight source folder (this repository), built once with mac/build.sh.

  1. Deploy the Worker (it opens the browser once to log in to Cloudflare):
cd companion/meeting-point
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy

It prints the address, like https://simsight.<your-account>.workers.dev. 2. Open SimSight setup (accessibility menu > companion setup, or double-click SimSight Setup.command in the Mods/SimSight folder), type that address under Meeting points, then Save. If the game was running, quit and restart it. 3. Start the game and load a household. Option+Command+A, phone companion: the QR code now opens the app at the meeting point, and the Mac says a 9-digit code. 4. On the phone: open the meeting point address, Share > Add to Home Screen, open the app from its icon and type the code (or scan the QR code in Safari first, then add it).

From then on: just open the app.

Another Mac: type the same meeting point in that Mac's SimSight setup; on the phone, Settings > Computers > Pair another computer, type the code that Mac says.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Update the Worker when you update the mod: the phone app lives there, so run npx wrangler deploy again after mac/build.sh. An old app with a newer mod may miss buttons.
  • Your own domain (optional): in the Cloudflare dashboard, Workers > simsight > Settings > Domains & Routes > add a custom domain such as sims-app.example.com. Use a different name from a fixed tunnel address (FIXED-ADDRESS.md) if you have one; the two do not need each other.
  • Free plan, no bill: a computer asks about 6 times an hour while the game runs, a phone once when it opens (more while it waits for the game). That is about 20 requests per player and evening; the free plan has 100,000 a day, and the app's files do not count. On the free plan, Cloudflare never charges: past the limit, the meeting point stops answering until the next day and the apps say so (see above).
  • Sharing yours: other players can list your address too. You then see their computers' IDs and tunnel addresses (not their names or games).
  • Turn it off: empty the meeting points on the setup page. Phones then use the computer's own link again (pair them again once).
  • Forget a phone or Mac: on the phone, Settings > Computers > Forget.

docs.title: SimSight Companion: player guide (phone companion)
docs.text: This guide explains, for players and for AI assistants helping them, how to play The Sims 4 on a Mac with SimSight Companion (the accessibility mod, based on TS4 Access) and its phone companion. It is written for blind and low-vision players using VoiceOver on an iPhone, often playing together with a sighted player on the Mac.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
• SimSight is an accessibility mod for The Sims 4, based on TS4 Access by tyjokr and LeonianUniverse. On the Mac, it reads what the mouse points at aloud and announces what the Sims do.
  • It also has a phone companion: a web app on the phone that shows the game and controls it. It is fully usable with VoiceOver.
  • Nothing is sent to a server of ours. The Mac runs a small local server; the phone reaches it through a temporary Cloudflare address (random, changes each time the game starts), or directly on the same Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Connecting the phone
docs.text:
1. Start the game on the Mac. When the Mac says "Phone link ready. Press Option Command A for the accessibility menu, then choose phone companion", it is ready.
  2. Press Option+Command+A: the SimSight menu opens with phone companion first; choose it (or click the accessibility icon in the macOS menu bar, then Phone companion…). A page with a QR code opens, and the Mac voice says a pairing code of 6 digits, 9 with a meeting point (said twice; it is also on the page).
  3. Scan the QR code with the phone camera and open the link in Safari. Or, without the camera: open the app (or the address) on the phone; on the Pair this phone screen, type the code in Pairing code (6 digits), then Pair with the code. A code works once, for 5 minutes, and after 5 wrong tries it stops: choose phone companion again for a new one.
  4. Optional: in Safari, Share > Add to Home Screen: the app opens full screen from its icon, already paired.
  5. The address changes each game session: scan again next time. The phone stays paired (it remembers its key). For an address that never changes (a Home Screen app that always works), see FIXED-ADDRESS.md, or MEETING-POINT.md (no domain needed, several Macs).
  6. Settings on the Mac side are on the SimSight setup page: accessibility menu > companion setup (or double-click SimSight Setup.command in the Mods/SimSight folder, game closed or not). It chooses the phone address (changing, fixed, or home Wi-Fi only), the meeting point, and Disconnect every phone if a phone is lost. Changes apply when the game starts. Under SimSight version it checks for updates: with the game running, the update is downloaded and installed when you quit the game; with the game closed, it is installed at once. At game start the Mac also says when a new version is out.
  7. With the game closed, the app still opens from the Home Screen and says the computer cannot be reached; it connects by itself once the game runs.

docs.title: Using the app with VoiceOver
docs.text:
• Swipe right from the top of the screen: first the Pause / Resume button (with the game speed, day and time), then the tabs, then the screen.
  • Use the VoiceOver rotor set to Headings to jump between sections.
  • Tabs: Live, Play, House, Sims, Settings, Help (two rows of three). History opens from Live with "Full history" (and has "Back to Live").
  • When the game asks a question, a card "The game asks: …" appears under the screen title on every tab, and VoiceOver announces it.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text:
• One button pauses the game, or resumes at the previous speed.
  • The four speeds (Pause, Play, Fast, Ultra fast) are in Play.

docs.title: Live
docs.text:
• Needs attention: what needs doing now, most urgent first:
  • low needs (hunger, bladder, energy, hygiene, fun, social);
  • fire, broken objects, puddles, spoiled food;
  • food ready to eat (cooked meals, deliveries): Eat, or Put away (the Sim takes it to the fridge);
  • visitors on the lot: Greet, Welcome;
  • bills due: Pay the bills (at the mailbox).
  • Each line has buttons that run the game's own actions:
  • Hunger: Eat now (quick meal from the fridge), Cook… (opens the recipe question), Other ways (fridge, stove, microwave, grill, and the phone to order food).
  • Bladder: Use the toilet. Energy: Sleep, Nap. Hygiene: Shower, Bath. Fun: Have fun (TV, computer...). Social: Call someone.
  • Broken object: Repair, or Hire a repair person (phone). Puddle: Mop it up, or Hire a maid. Spoiled food: Throw it away. Fire: Put out the fire, or Call the firefighters.
  • For a Sim that is not the controlled one, the button is "Control " first: actions always run for the controlled Sim.
  • Then: the Mac voice switch, the household (funds, mood), and the latest events. "Full history" opens History.

docs.title: Play
docs.text: From top to bottom: - Controlled Sim: one button per Sim on the lot; the pressed one is the Sim you play. Actions always run for this Sim. - 's actions: the action running now and the ones waiting in the queue, each with a Cancel button (as in the game, only for the controlled Sim). The Sims tab shows every Sim's queue too. - 's inventory (in You): what the Sim carries ("Food: Mac and Cheese ×2"), each with "Put in Fridge, 3 m" buttons, one per place on the lot that accepts it (several fridges: each one). One tap moves the whole stack, like dragging it in the game. - You: the Sim itself (self-care, its own interactions) and the Sim's phone (calls, invitations, going out, services, travel). - Interact: - Search by type or name, in English, French or Spanish ("fridge", "frigo", "nevera", "shower", "douche", "ducha"...). Several words narrow the search. The keyboard's Search key closes the keyboard and goes to the results; the number found is announced. - Sims nearby, closest first. - Objects by category (Appliances, Plumbing, Comfort, Surfaces, Electronics, Activities, Kids, Storage... Decorations, Lighting and Build last). Categories are folded: each is a button "Appliances, 3" that opens it. A search opens every category with results. - Choose a Sim or object: its menu is the game's own pie menu, with categories. Unavailable rows say why ("Lobster, unavailable: requires Cooking level 9"). Choosing a row adds the action to the Sim's queue. - Camera: moves the game camera on the Mac to the controlled Sim: Follow , Close-up on , and Free camera to let go. Useful to hear the Sims talk. - Game speed: Pause, Play, Fast, Ultra fast.

docs.title: House
docs.text:
• The home floor by floor (ground floor, floor 1, basement).
  • Each room is named from its furniture (Kitchen, Bathroom, Bedroom, Living room, Dining room, Study, Nursery, Room), with its part of the floor (north-west part, middle...), size in metres, and distance and direction from the controlled Sim. North is the game's north.
  • A room shows: doors and openings to other rooms and outside (each opens that room), who is inside, and what is in it with where (north side, middle...). Decorations and lights are grouped separately. Objects open their menu.
  • The garden ("Outside") and pools are listed like rooms.
  • Each floor says where its stairs are ("Stairs up to Floor 1: east part, in the Living room"); rooms with stairs list "Stairs up to …" / "Stairs down to …" in their ways in and out.
  • An open-plan space is named by both parts ("Kitchen and Living room") and says where each part is ("Kitchen area: north side").
  • Live and Sims say which room each Sim is in.

docs.title: Sims
docs.text:
• Each household Sim: job and work performance (towards the next promotion), mood, needs (lowest first), moodlets with time left, the action queue (actions can be cancelled), skills (level of 10), relationships (friendship and romance from -100 to 100, with labels like "Good Friends", "Spouse").
  • Sims at work or school say where they are and until when.
  • Goals: the aspiration and its current milestone with each step (done or to do), wants and fears, today's work tasks, and what the next promotion needs.

docs.title: History
docs.text: • Every event, newest first.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
• App language (French, English, Spanish). Names from the game stay in the game's language.
  • What VoiceOver announces automatically: game messages and questions, mood changes, new moodlets, low needs, actions starting, speed and money.
  • Pause while I choose an action (off by default): the game pauses when a menu opens and resumes once the action is queued or the menu closes.
  • Mac voice: hover reading on/off, Sim action announcements on/off.
  • Conversations: off, only new relationship levels, what they do and how it goes (default), or everything.
  • The Mac voice announces: the same choices, for the Mac's own voice (kept on the Mac, for playing without the phone). By default moods, low needs and new relationship levels; the mod already reads game windows and notifications itself.
  • Unpair this phone.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: • This guide, in the app's language.

docs.title: On the Mac
docs.text:
• Option+Command+S: speech on/off (also while the game has focus).
  • Option+Command+A: the SimSight menu.
  • Accessibility icon in the macOS menu bar: the same, plus Phone companion….
  • Cheat console (Cmd+Shift+C): simsight.hub (menu), simsight.companion (QR code).
  • The original mod's keyboard works too, with Mac keys (Control+Shift for its Ctrl+Alt keys, Option+Shift for its Alt keys): see KEYBOARD.md.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Bella can't do “Take Shower”: no way to get there, check doors and stairs": the Sim could not reach the place (the game shows a "blocked" bubble). Add a door or stairs, or move what is in the way. Said on the Mac and on the phone.
  • "Waiting for the game": the game is loading or closed.
  • The page does not open: the game was restarted, so the address changed. Scan the new QR code.
  • An action is missing from a menu: the game does not offer it right now (wrong place, Sim busy, needs a skill). Try Refresh in Play.
  • Quick action says "Nothing nearby can do it": open Other ways.
  • Direct Wi-Fi test (no internet needed): on the Mac, run mac/wifi-test.sh, scan the QR code; it says when the phone connects.

docs.title: For AI assistants
docs.text:
• Answer in the player's language. The player may be blind: give step-by-step instructions in terms of VoiceOver swipes, headings and button names as written above, not colours or positions on screen.
  • Game object and action names come from the game (usually English).
  • Source code: https://github.com/the40n8/simsight-companion (phone app in companion/web, game side in Scripts/simsight_bridge.py).

docs.title: Plugin spec: SimSight Companion helper
docs.text: Specification for ChatGPT's Plugin Creator. To create the plugin, send it this file's link: https://github.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/blob/main/docs/mac/PLUGIN.md

docs.title: Name and purpose
docs.text:
• Name: SimSight Companion helper
  • Description: Help with SimSight on Mac: the Sims 4 accessibility mod and its phone app for VoiceOver. Answers in your language.
  • Purpose: answer questions about playing The Sims 4 on a Mac with the SimSight accessibility mod and its phone companion app, for players who are often blind or low vision and use VoiceOver on an iPhone (a sighted player often plays on the Mac at the same time). It explains how to do things in the app and the game, step by step, in the user's language.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
When to use: any question about SimSight, its phone companion app ("Live", "Play", "House", "Sims", "Settings", "Help" screens), its Mac shortcuts, installing it, or playing The Sims 4 with it.

Steps:

  1. At the start of every conversation, before answering, read the current guides (they change often; never answer from memory):
  2. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/llms.txt
  3. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/docs/mac/PHONE-GUIDE.md Then read the other files listed in llms.txt when the question needs them (keyboard: docs/mac/KEYBOARD.md; installing: mac/PLAYERS.md; fixed phone address: docs/mac/FIXED-ADDRESS.md; testing and reporting problems: docs/mac/TESTING.md).
  4. If the guides cannot be opened, say so, use the reference files bundled with the plugin if there are any (and say the answer might be out of date), otherwise answer carefully and mark what is uncertain.
  5. Answer:
  6. in the user's language (often Spanish or French); keep the app's screen and button names as the app shows them in that language when known, otherwise give the English name in quotes;
  7. in short numbered steps a screen reader user can follow: screen (tab) names, headings, button names, swipes ("swipe right to the button …, double-tap"); never colours, icons or positions on screen;
  8. one task at a time; ask what they hear or see if something does not match the guide.
  9. Game object and action names come from the game, usually in English ("Quick Meal", "Grab a Plate").
  10. Problems the guide does not cover: point to its "When something goes wrong" section, or suggest reporting the problem to the person who installed the mod.

Rules:

  • Do not invent features: if the guides do not mention something, say it is not in the app yet.
  • Never ask for or repeat pairing links, tokens or the contents of config.json: they are private keys to the game.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• Web browsing / web search to read the public guides above from GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com). No account, API key or private data needed.
  • If plugins cannot browse: bundle these files as reference files instead, and tell the plugin owner they must be re-uploaded when the guides change: llms.txt, docs/mac/PHONE-GUIDE.md, docs/mac/KEYBOARD.md, mac/PLAYERS.md (same raw.githubusercontent.com/the40n8/simsight-companion/main/ base).
  • No other apps, tools or services.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. "How do I start playing with the phone app?" Expected: numbered steps from the guide's "Connecting the phone": start the game, wait for "Phone link ready", Option+Command+A then phone companion, scan the QR code, then the Live screen; mentions swiping right from the top (Pause button, then the tabs).
  2. "¿Cómo hago que mi Sim coma?" Expected, in Spanish: the "Needs attention" card on the Live screen (En directo) with its Eat now / Cook buttons when Hunger is low, or Play > search "nevera" > open the fridge > choose an action; a recipe question appears as "El juego pregunta" with its choices.
  3. "Comment savoir où sont les pièces de la maison ?" Expected, in French: the House screen (Maison): floors, rooms with their part of the floor and size, open a room to hear its doors, stairs and what is inside; north is the game's north.

Test: after creating it, ask example 1. The answer should name the Live, Play or House screens and say it read the guide.

docs.title: Test checklist (Mac and phone app)
docs.text: For a play session: try each line, and note what happened when it does not match. Lines marked new have only been checked outside the game so far. Install the latest build first (mac/install.sh, game closed).

docs.title: How to report a problem
docs.text:
For each problem, note: 1. Where: the screen (Live, Play, House, Sims, Settings, Help) or the Mac. 2. What you did: the buttons or keys, in order. 3. What happened: what VoiceOver or the Mac said, word for word if you can. 4. What you expected. 5. When: the game time or a rough clock time (it helps find the log line).

Example: "Play > Fridge > Cook. The question 'What should Bella cook?' did not appear on the phone; the Mac showed it. 21:40."

docs.title: Starting
docs.text:
• [ ] Game loads a household; the Mac says "Phone link ready. Press Option Command A…" once you are in the house (not at the main menu). new
  • [ ] Option+Command+A opens the SimSight menu, phone companion first, then the new grouped menu (yourself, needs, Sims, places…).
  • [ ] Phone companion shows the QR code; the phone opens the app.
  • [ ] Phone companion: the Mac says a 6-digit code; typed on the Pair this phone screen, it pairs the phone (a wrong code is refused).
  • [ ] Meeting point (if set up): the Home Screen app says "Waiting for the game" with the game closed, and connects by itself once it is loaded.
  • [ ] Option+Command+S turns the Mac voice off and on ("Speech off" / "Speech on").

docs.title: Top bar and tabs
docs.text:
• [ ] First on screen: Pause (or Resume) with the speed and the time; it pauses and resumes at the previous speed. VoiceOver stays on the button.
  • [ ] Six tabs in two rows; Help opens; long text does not run off the screen.

docs.title: Live: Needs attention new
docs.text:
• [ ] A low need appears with buttons (Eat now, Cook…, Sleep, Shower…).
  • [ ] Eat now queues a quick meal from the fridge; Cook… opens the recipe question on the phone.
  • [ ] A broken object, a puddle, spoiled food or food ready shows up, and its button works (Repair, Mop it up, Throw it away, Eat).
  • [ ] A visitor on the lot: Greet / Welcome work.
  • [ ] Bills due: Pay the bills pays them at the mailbox.
  • [ ] A Sim you do not control shows "Control " first.
  • [ ] Each Sim line says which room the Sim is in.

docs.title: Game questions on the phone new
docs.text:
• [ ] A question with buttons (OK / Cancel or custom) appears on every tab as "The game asks: …" and is announced; answering it works in the game.
  • [ ] A list to pick from (recipe, guests, food to order): rows read well, greyed rows say why, OK works only after choosing.
  • [ ] A text box (naming something): typing and OK work.
  • [ ] Corner notifications are announced and listed in History.

docs.title: Play
docs.text:
• [ ] Order: Controlled Sim, the Sim's actions (Cancel works), Camera, You (yourself and the phone), Interact, Game speed.
  • [ ] Search "frigo" / "nevera" / "fridge"; the keyboard's Search key closes the keyboard and goes to the results.
  • [ ] Categories open and close; items are inside.
  • [ ] An object's menu lists the game's actions (not "No actions"); choosing one queues it.
  • [ ] The Sim's phone menu: call someone, invite over, order food. new
  • [ ] Camera: Follow, Close-up, Free camera move the Mac's camera. new
  • [ ] Settings > "Pause while I choose an action": pauses on opening a menu, resumes after queuing.

docs.title: House new
docs.text:
• [ ] Rooms are named sensibly (kitchen, bathroom, bedroom…), with size and where they are on the floor.
  • [ ] Doors and openings link the right rooms; tapping one opens that room.
  • [ ] Stairs: each floor says where they are; rooms list "Stairs up/down".
  • [ ] An open kitchen and living room is named by both and says which part is where.
  • [ ] Garden and pool appear with what is in them.

docs.title: Sims new
docs.text:
• [ ] Work performance, skills, relationships (with labels) look right.
  • [ ] Goals: aspiration and milestone steps, wants and fears, work tasks, promotion steps.

docs.title: Conversations and announcements new
docs.text:
• [ ] A chat between Sims gives "Bella and Nancy: Chat, friendship +3."
  • [ ] A new relationship level gives "now Friends" (or similar).
  • [ ] Settings > Conversations changes how much is announced.
  • [ ] Settings > The Mac voice announces: ticked kinds are said by the Mac, not when the Mac voice is off.

docs.title: Mac keyboard new
docs.text: Only while the game is the front app (see KEYBOARD.md): - [ ] Control+Shift+H (menu), +C (time), +Q (queue), +N (needs), +1/2 (switch Sims). - [ ] Option+Shift+T (time), +N (needs), +R (rooms), +W (where am I). - [ ] With keyboard navigation on (SimSight settings): arrows, Tab, Enter, Esc move through an open menu or dialog with speech; outside menus the game keeps its keys. - [ ] Other apps keep their shortcuts while the game is in the background.

docs.title: Ask an AI
docs.text: • [ ] Help > Ask an AI > Open ChatGPT: the request is filled in and the answer follows the guide in your language.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Alpha: not yet tried inside the game

The installer, the phone companion and the speech through NVDA are tested on Windows 11. The mod itself has not been played on Windows with this release yet. Its Windows parts (speech, keyboard, scanner) come unchanged from TS4 Access. Testers are wanted.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Install with one PowerShell line, the game closed.
  2. Start your screen reader (NVDA or JAWS; Narrator is not supported), then The Sims 4 through the EA app or Steam, and load a household.
  3. Press Control+Alt+H for the accessibility menu. In settings, turn Scanner mode on (or press Control+Alt+Space).
  4. Wait for "Scanner", then browse with the arrows: Up and Down move in the list, Right enters a category, Left or Backspace goes back, Enter opens the interactions, Space repeats.

Your screen reader speaks for the mod and keeps its own voice and speed. Without one, a Windows voice is used.

docs.title: The phone app
docs.text:
In the accessibility menu, choose phone companion: a page with a QR code opens in the browser, and your screen reader says a pairing code. Scan the QR code with the phone, or type the code in the app. The pairing page also has Copy link and Share to send the link to your phone.

Then read the phone guide: it is the same app on Mac and Windows. Settings for the phone link (a fixed address, meeting points, disconnecting every phone) and updates are in the accessibility menu under companion setup; with the game closed, open SimSight Setup.cmd in Mods\SimSight.

docs.title: Full guides
docs.text:
These plain text guides are also in your Mods\SimSight folder:

  • README.txt: getting started, settings, simplified menus, travel, households, Build mode, current limitations.
  • CONTROLS.txt: every keyboard shortcut, by activity.
  • CHEATS.txt: optional settings and help commands.
